# Linear Algebra — analogies

## [Linear maps](linear-maps.md)
- A linear map is a machine that doesn't care whether you add inputs before or after feeding them in.

## [Image](linear-maps/image.md)
- The image is the set of places the machine can actually produce, regardless of what you feed it.

## [Kernel](linear-maps/kernel.md)
- The kernel is the shadow of what T flattens away. Everything in it lands on the same point.

## [Vector spaces](vector-spaces.md)
- A vector space is a game board with two legal moves. A subspace is a region you can never leave using those moves.

## [Basis](vector-spaces/basis.md)
- A basis is a coordinate system with no redundant axes and no missing ones.

## [Span](vector-spaces/span.md)
- Span is everywhere you can reach by walking along the given directions for any distance, forwards or backwards.
